details:
AstroTrack — Autonomous Astronaut Health Monitoring System

AstroTrack is an astronaut health monitoring and decision-support platform designed to help monitor human health during long-duration space missions. Astronauts operating in space face unique physiological and psychological challenges due to microgravity, disrupted sleep cycles, isolation, and demanding mission conditions. Continuous health monitoring can help identify unusual patterns early and support better-informed health decisions.

AstroTrack brings multiple health indicators together in a centralized dashboard. It monitors seven key indicators: heart rate, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, body temperature, blood glucose, sleep duration, and mood. The platform presents health readings, historical trends, and status indicators to make potentially concerning changes easier to recognize.

An AI-powered explanation feature provides accessible explanations of health observations and suggested next steps, helping users understand why a particular reading or pattern may deserve attention. The system is designed as a decision-support prototype, not a replacement for medical professionals or a clinically validated diagnostic tool.

Benefits and Intended Impact

AstroTrack aims to support astronaut well-being by making health information easier to monitor, understand, and interpret. By combining physiological and behavioral indicators, it provides a broader view of an astronaut's health rather than treating individual measurements in isolation. Its intended impact is to contribute to early awareness of potential health concerns, support mission health management, and encourage the development of more intelligent health-monitoring solutions for future long-duration missions.

Technology and Tools

The project was developed using:

  • Frontend: Next.js, React, TypeScript, and Tailwind CSS.
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI.
  • Database: PostgreSQL.
  • Data visualization: Recharts.
  • AI integration: AI-powered health explanations.
  • Development tools: Git, GitHub, Docker, and Vercel.

The current demonstration uses simulated mission telemetry to demonstrate the monitoring, visualization, and explanation workflows. These readings are synthetic demonstration data, not live astronaut sensor measurements.

Creativity and Design Considerations

AstroTrack combines multiple dimensions of astronaut health into one monitoring experience. Its creative approach is the integration of physiological measurements, sleep, and mood with historical trends and AI-assisted explanations. We considered usability, clarity of health information, accessibility, modularity, and the limitations of interpreting health measurements in a spaceflight environment.

Our goal is to make complex health information easier to understand while providing a foundation that could be extended with real spaceflight research datasets, validated medical reference standards, and future sensor integrations.
